claims.text: Air annealing Q235 at approximately 700 °C for 1–10 hours will form a reproducible surface oxide scale.
The pre-formed Q235 scale will be continuous and enriched in Mn and Si oxides.
The annealed scale will consist of iron oxides mixed with minor Mn- and Si-containing oxide phases.
High-temperature annealing selectively oxidizes Mn and Si at the Q235 surface.
Selective oxidation of Mn and Si makes the Q235 oxide scale more continuous and adherent.
A continuous and adherent pre-formed oxide scale acts as a diffusion barrier to corrosive species during molten-salt exposure.
The proposed diffusion barrier limits further high-temperature oxidation and degradation.
At room temperature, the pre-formed scale may be less protective because its phase stability and adhesion differ from those under hot-corrosion conditions.
Pre-annealed Q235 will show lower mass change than untreated Q235 during molten-salt corrosion at 700–900 °C.
Pre-annealed Q235 will show less spallation or pitting than untreated Q235 during molten-salt corrosion at 700–900 °C.
The pre-annealing treatment will provide weak or no corrosion benefit at room temperature.
Protection requires the pre-annealing treatment to produce a continuous, adherent oxide layer.
An annealing duration that is too short will produce insufficient scale, whereas excessive annealing can thicken the scale and promote spallation.
The proposed protective mechanism is expected to be significant in aggressive high-temperature molten salts but not necessarily in lower-temperature corrosion regimes.
The controlled study will compare air-annealed and untreated Q235 using mass change, XRD, SEM/EDS, scale thickness, spallation, and pitting measurements.

contradictions.description: The boundary states that the mechanism may not apply when annealing fails to produce a continuous, adherent scale, but the falsification rule treats absence of enhanced continuity or adhesion together with absent protection as falsification. Under the stated boundary, that result could instead mean that the intervention failed to instantiate the hypothesized mediator.
